findings: Fix cycle round 2 for #84 addressed all 4 Majors and all 6 minors from review round 1 (REJECT), landed at commit baf109e on car/adapter-84 (base bc552df). R1-M1: lastGoodAsOf/lastGoodLaneData["freight"] now gated on freightFreshnessVal != never-polled in poll.go, red-before/green-after in poll_test.go plus a real-browser regression reproducing the reviewer's exact "showing last good" string via fault injection then correcting it, restore sha256-verified as a separate step after one mid-round mistake (a stale backup silently reverted round-2 work, caught via git diff before any further claim was made, redone and reverified). R1-M2: a new freight-tickets-without-heartbeat board condition (TierFlag) fires when tickets exist with no heartbeat, red-before/green-after with a positive and negative control test plus a real-browser regression asserting the board-conditions strip discloses the code by name. R1-M3: all five screenshot directories opened and every image observed directly (not assumed) - two previously uncaptioned files (first-light.png, view-67-candidates/lane-filters.png) got new READMEs, three existing Status:-Current READMEs got DISCLOSED DIVERGENCE sections scoped to exactly the images that show FREIGHT/Dark (6 of 8 in the 69-71 directory, not all 8), and one caption was self-corrected in place after re-opening an image disproved an assumption in an earlier draft. R1-M4: Sync-Freight.ps1's header corrected from the measured-false "writes NOTHING" claim to describe the actual non-atomic partial-write behavior and explain why R1-M2's board-side detection is the actual safety net; chose to correct the header rather than rewrite the store to be atomic, reasoning stated (atomicity would require a structural store-layout change touching recordDir conventions other lanes depend on, out of fix-cycle scope, while R1-M2 already closes the reader-visible defect); a new red-first test reaches a genuine mid-run failure through the script's real public interface (a blocking file), never a code injection. All six minors (m1-m6) fixed: snapshot.go's stale Lane doc comment corrected with its lanes.js citation verified still resolving; node count instrument reporting reconciled to one number (238/238, trailer and per-test agree); dom-writer.js's renderFreight now renders recordDir as a provenance link distinct from the title's issue-URL link, red-before/green-after with sha256-verified restore; docs/setup.md documents both the adapter's manual invocation and a disclosed, deliberately undecided scheduling gap; StoreIntegrity.Tests.ps1 gained a ticket-schema Context mirroring the existing manifest one; index.md non-regeneration is now named explicitly in both the adapter's header and the state ledger's Question 2, within issue #20's already-landed contract. Suite arithmetic at final HEAD, one instrument each: Go board 111/111 PASS 0 FAIL (was 108), go vet and go fmt clean; board/web node 238/238 (trailer and per-test count agree, was 234); Pester scripts/tests 236 pass 0 fail 4 skip of 240 (was 235/0/4/239); scripts/probes 29/29 unchanged; scripts/store-checks 275/275 (was 271, +4). Isolated re-runs of browser-freight-states.test.js (5/5) and browser-dispatch-row-geometry.test.js (3/3) confirm no regression.
abstract: Round 2 fix cycle for issue #84 (freight lane adapter) closed all four Majors and six minors from the round-1 REJECT verdict. Both Law-1 findings (a never-run lane falsely claiming last-good data after a scan failure, and tickets rendering beside a false "not yet polled" with no board condition) are fixed with red-first Go tests plus real-browser regressions that reproduce the reviewer's own measured evidence via fault injection before confirming the fix. The screenshot audit was extended beyond the reviewer's three cited images to all five directories, finding and fixing two additional uncaptioned files and self-correcting one caption after re-opening the image it described. The adapter's own documented failure contract was corrected to match its measured behavior rather than reasserting a false claim, with the board-side R1-M2 fix carrying the actual safety guarantee. One process mistake (a stale-backup restore that silently reverted round-2 work) was caught mid-round via diff inspection, disclosed, and corrected before any further claim was built on top of it. All suites green at the final commit.
